newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. asks water suppliers to join clean-up program.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. asks water suppliers to join clean-up program.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki Monday asked water suppliers to submit applications for the state's first safe drinking water program, which will spend $1.87 billion of federal and state money money over 10 years.
The revolving loan fund will get around $355 million of bonds from the 1996 Clean Water/Clean Air Bond Act that was approved by voters in the November elections.
A spokeswoman for the Environmental Facilities Corp said the bonds will be sold over a number of years.
She referred inquiries about when the bond sales would begin to the state division of budget, which was not immediately available to comment.

During the campaign for the green bond, one of the main controversies focused on the Administration's lack of a specific list of projects that would be approved. The governor said statewide public hearings would be held in January on how eligible projects would be prioritized and on the criteria that would be used for financially disadvantaged areas.
From the pre-applications, which interested water suppliers have been asked to submit by February 1, the Department of Health will develop a yearly intended use plan.

Noting more than 16 million New Yorkers get their drinking water from 4,000 suppliers, Pataki said, "The money from this fund will ensure that our children grow up with safe, high quality drinking water."
